nonAffiliation: These are our own practice questions. They are not the questions used in the real test, and this app is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by the Australian Government or the Department of Home Affairs. Home Affairs says of its own sample test that the questions will be different on the day.
disclosure: Australia does not publish the questions used in the citizenship test - Home Affairs publishes a twenty-question sample and says the real questions will be different on the day. These are practice questions we wrote, and each one tests a fact stated in the testable section of Australian Citizenship: Our Common Bond, the free official booklet, which is the material the real test is drawn from. Every question records the part of the booklet it came from.

valuesRule.note: All five Australian values questions must be answered correctly, as well as an overall mark of at least 15 out of 20. Missing one values question means not passing, whatever the overall mark.

questions.question: Who are Australia's first inhabitants?
options: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
answers: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

questions.question: Whose cultures and traditions are the oldest continuous ones in the world?
options: The Torres Strait Islander peoples' alone
The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples'
answers: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples'

questions.question: Where are the Torres Strait Islander people from?
options: Islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea
answers: Islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea

questions.question: On what date did the First Fleet arrive from Great Britain?
answers: 26 January 1788

questions.question: What was the First Fleet?
options: The first 11 convict ships to arrive from Great Britain
The fleet that discovered the Torres Strait
The ships that carried gold to Britain
The first free settlers' ships from Ireland
answers: The first 11 convict ships to arrive from Great Britain

questions.question: Who was the first Governor of the colony of New South Wales?
answers: Captain Arthur Phillip

questions.question: Why did the British Government decide to transport convicts to New South Wales?
options: British laws were harsh and the jails could not hold everyone imprisoned
To find gold for the Crown
To defend the colony against invasion
To build the Sydney Harbour Bridge
answers: British laws were harsh and the jails could not hold everyone imprisoned

questions.question: In which year did a gold rush begin in the colonies of New South Wales and Victoria?
Which was the first colony established by the British in Australia?
answers: New South Wales

questions.question: How many states and mainland territories does the Commonwealth of Australia have?
options: Six states and two mainland territories
Five states and three mainland territories
answers: Six states and two mainland territories

questions.question: Which city is the capital of both Australia and the Australian Capital Territory?
answers: Canberra

questions.question: Which is Australia's largest city?
answers: Sydney

questions.question: What is the capital city of Victoria?
answers: Melbourne

questions.question: What is the capital city of Queensland?
answers: Brisbane

questions.question: What is the capital city of Western Australia?
answers: Perth

questions.question: What is the capital city of South Australia?
answers: Adelaide

questions.question: What is the capital city of Tasmania?
answers: Hobart

questions.question: What is the capital city of the Northern Territory?
answers: Darwin

questions.question: Which flag is the official flag of Australia?
answers: The Australian National Flag

questions.question: What are the three colours of the Australian National Flag?
answers: Blue, white and red

questions.question: What sits in the top left corner of the Australian National Flag?
options: The Union Jack, the flag of the United Kingdom
answers: The Union Jack, the flag of the United Kingdom

questions.question: How many points does the Commonwealth Star on the flag have, and why?
options: Eight - one for each state and territory
Five - one for each original colony
Seven - one for each of the six states and one for the territories
answers: Seven - one for each of the six states and one for the territories

questions.question: What is the group of stars on the right of the Australian National Flag?
answers: The Southern Cross

questions.question: What does the yellow circle on the Australian Aboriginal Flag represent?
answers: The sun

questions.question: What does the white dancer's headdress in the centre of the Torres Strait Islander Flag symbolise?
answers: All Torres Strait Islanders

questions.question: What is the official symbol of the Commonwealth of Australia?
answers: The Commonwealth Coat of Arms

questions.question: Which two native animals support the shield on the Commonwealth Coat of Arms?
answers: A kangaroo and an emu

questions.question: What is Australia's national anthem?
answers: Advance Australia Fair

categories.section: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: What kind of system of government does Australia have?
answers: A parliamentary democracy
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: In Australia's system of government, where does the power of the government come from?
options: The Australian people, because citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament
answers: The Australian people, because citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: What does the Rule of Law mean?
options: The government is not bound by the laws it passes
No person, group or religious rule is above the law
Only citizens are required to obey the law
Judges may set aside a law they disagree with
answers: No person, group or religious rule is above the law
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: Who must obey Australia's laws?
options: Everyone, including government, community and religious leaders, business people and the police
answers: Everyone, including government, community and religious leaders, business people and the police
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: How do Australians believe change should occur?
options: Through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process
Through the decisions of religious leaders
Through protest that may include violence if a cause is just
answers: Through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: What does freedom of speech allow people in Australia to do?
options: Say and write what they think and discuss their ideas, while still obeying Australian laws
Say anything at all, with no limits
Criticise the government only in private
Publish opinions only if they are true
answers: Say and write what they think and discuss their ideas, while still obeying Australian laws
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: What is freedom of association?
options: The right to practise any religion
The right to form and join associations to pursue common goals
The right to say what you think
The right to move freely between states
answers: The right to form and join associations to pursue common goals
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: What does freedom of expression cover?
options: Expressing views through art, film, music and literature
answers: Expressing views through art, film, music and literature
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: Which of these is an Australian democratic belief?
options: Preference for the wealthy in courts of law
Obedience to religious leaders above the law
Respect for all individuals regardless of background
answers: Respect for all individuals regardless of background
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

questions.question: How are Australians expected to treat one another?
options: With dignity and respect, regardless of background
According to their standing in the community
answers: With dignity and respect, regardless of background
questions.guideSection: Part 2 - Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties

categories.section: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: On what date did the Australian colonies unite into a federation?
answers: 1 January 1901
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is the name of the federation the colonies became?
answers: The Commonwealth of Australia
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is the Australian Constitution?
options: A list of the rights of every Australian citizen
An agreement between the states and the United Kingdom
The legal document that sets out the basic rules for the government of Australia
The Act that created the High Court only
answers: The legal document that sets out the basic rules for the government of Australia
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What did the Australian Constitution establish?
options: The office of Prime Minister and the Cabinet
The Parliament of the Commonwealth of Australia and the High Court of Australia
answers: The Parliament of the Commonwealth of Australia and the High Court of Australia
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: Which court has the ultimate power to apply and interpret the laws of Australia?
options: The Supreme Court of New South Wales
answers: The High Court of Australia
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How can the Australian people change the Australian Constitution?
options: By a decision of the High Court
By a proclamation of the Governor-General
By a vote of the House of Representatives alone
answers: By voting in a referendum
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is the 'double majority' needed to change the Australian Constitution?
options: A majority of voters in every state
Two-thirds of voters across the nation
A majority of voters in a majority of states, and a majority of voters across the nation
A majority in both Houses of Parliament
answers: A majority of voters in a majority of states, and a majority of voters across the nation
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What did more than 90 per cent of Australians vote 'Yes' to in the 1967 Referendum?
options: Adopting Advance Australia Fair as the anthem
Allowing Aboriginal peoples to be counted in the Census
answers: Allowing Aboriginal peoples to be counted in the Census
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How does the Australian Constitution stop one person or group from holding all the power?
options: It limits the Prime Minister to two terms
It requires elections every three years
It divides power between the legislative, executive and judicial powers
It gives the High Court power over parliament
answers: It divides power between the legislative, executive and judicial powers
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is legislative power?
options: The power to put laws into practice
The power to interpret and apply the law
answers: The power to make laws
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is executive power?
options: The power to change the Constitution
The power to interpret the law
The power to put the laws into practice
answers: The power to put the laws into practice
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: Who holds judicial power in Australia?
options: Judges, who interpret and apply the law
The Prime Minister and the Cabinet
answers: Judges, who interpret and apply the law
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: Which two Houses make up the Australian Parliament?
options: The House of Representatives and the High Court
The House of Commons and the Senate
The Lower House and the Cabinet
The House of Representatives and the Senate
answers: The House of Representatives and the Senate
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: By what other names is the House of Representatives known?
options: The Upper House or the States' House
The Lower House or the People's House
answers: The Lower House or the People's House
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: By what other names is the Senate known?
options: The Upper House, the House of Review or the States' House
The Lower House or the People's House
answers: The Upper House, the House of Review or the States' House
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How many senators are there in total?
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How many senators does each state elect?
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How many senators do the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory each elect?
answers: Two
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How is the number of members of the House of Representatives for each state and territory decided?
options: By the number of people in that state or territory
By the size of the state's area
answers: By the number of people in that state or territory
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: How are all the states represented in the Senate?
options: Equally, regardless of their size or population
answers: Equally, regardless of their size or population
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is the leader of a state government called?
answers: The Premier
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What is the leader of a territory government called?
answers: The Chief Minister
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: Who is the Sovereign's representative in Australia, and on whose advice are they appointed?
options: The Governor of New South Wales, appointed by the states
The Governor-General, appointed on the advice of the Australian Prime Minister
The Chief Justice, appointed on the advice of the Cabinet
The Prime Minister, appointed on the advice of parliament
answers: The Governor-General, appointed on the advice of the Australian Prime Minister
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: In which elections is voting compulsory in Australia?
options: No elections; voting is always voluntary
Federal and state or territory elections
answers: Federal and state or territory elections
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What does each state government have of its own?
options: Its own currency and defence force
answers: Its own parliament and constitution
questions.guideSection: Part 3 - Government and the law in Australia

questions.question: What does Australian society value about the rights of all people?
options: The rights of the community above those of the individual
Their equal rights, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, race or origin
The rights of citizens above those of residents
The rights of those born in Australia above those of migrants
answers: Their equal rights, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, race or origin

questions.question: In Australia, what does the law say about marriage between two men or two women?
options: It requires the approval of a court
Two people can marry each other, including two men or two women
Marriage is only between a man and a woman
answers: Two people can marry each other, including two men or two women

questions.question: What rights do men and women have in Australia?
options: Women have priority in family matters
Equal rights, with equality of opportunity to pursue their goals and interests
answers: Equal rights, with equality of opportunity to pursue their goals and interests

questions.question: What is the position of physical violence against a spouse or partner in Australia?
options: It is never acceptable and is a criminal offence
It is only an offence if reported by a doctor
It is a private family matter
It is dealt with by community leaders
answers: It is never acceptable and is a criminal offence

questions.question: Who may apply to the courts for a divorce in Australia?
options: Only with the agreement of both spouses
Only after approval by a religious authority
Either a husband or a wife, even if the other spouse wishes to continue the marriage
answers: Either a husband or a wife, even if the other spouse wishes to continue the marriage

questions.question: What does a 'fair go' mean in Australia?
options: Everyone, regardless of background, has an equal opportunity to achieve success in life
Everyone is given a government job if they need one
People of the same class are treated alike
answers: Everyone, regardless of background, has an equal opportunity to achieve success in life

questions.question: On what basis should a person get a job in Australia?
answers: Their skills and experience

questions.question: What should what someone achieves in life be the result of?
options: The class they were born into
answers: Their hard work and talents

questions.question: Do people of different faiths receive different treatment under Australian law?
options: Yes - it depends on the state
Yes - only recognised religions are protected
No - people of all faiths receive the same treatment
answers: No - people of all faiths receive the same treatment

questions.question: Is it lawful in Australia to treat someone differently because of their gender?
options: No - it is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender
Yes, where a job has always been done by one gender
answers: No - it is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender

questions.question: What rights do men and women have over personal matters such as marriage and religion?
options: The head of the household decides
Parents decide until the age of 25
Both have the right to make their own independent choices, protected from intimidation or violence
answers: Both have the right to make their own independent choices, protected from intimidation or violence

questions.question: What access do both men and women have to education and employment?
options: Equal access, and both may vote, stand for parliament and join the Defence Force and police
answers: Equal access, and both may vote, stand for parliament and join the Defence Force and police
